gates.evidence: Proposal targets investigative deep-dive articles in a news feed; surface is SFW.
Reward is access to a specific premium article, not for clicks or installs.
Proposal introduces an additive tier; no existing free content is removed.
Uses modal ns1 with a distinct 'Play Now' button.
Body text clearly states: 'Play a 15-second game to access this in-depth investigative article.'
Offer includes a 'No thanks' button as an equally legible decline option.
Triggered upon navigation (tapping an article), not mid-reading.
Proposal explicitly targets returning non-subscribing users.

scores.evidence: Triggering the reward exactly when the user expresses intent by tapping a 'Premium' article is a high-intent match.
The model is additive ('zero free content removed'), preserving the integrity of the existing news feed.
The 'wait or watch' model is rate-limited (3/day) and additive, avoiding subscription cannibalization.
COGS is near zero (content), and revenue per view is positive; well within limits.
Reach is limited to the volume of 'Premium' articles created; could be low if content is sparse.
Uses standard SIM-RWD; requires new backend support for gating specific content, which is a moderate engineering task.
Uses AOL nouns like 'Home News Feed' and 'AOL News' as game partner, but the core mechanics are standard.
Includes a 3-per-day cap and 30-minute cooldown, preventing over-exposure.
Explicit KPIs, guardrails, and a user-level holdout plan provided.

requiredChanges: Grounding: Update proposal to acknowledge that 'PremiumAccess' is a new, non-existent resource, requiring infrastructure to track and gate specific premium content.
Editorial Strategy: Clarify how 'Premium' articles will be curated or distinguished in the feed to ensure they are high-value enough to justify the ad break.
parsed.topConcern: The lack of existing infrastructure (economy, content gating) to support the proposed Premium tier requires significant backend work that is not yet detailed.
